A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EBLoRA research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison after matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original continual-learning evaluations, adapter-merging experiments, interference tests, and component ablations, including detailed appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds free-spectrum comparisons, computational-cost measurements, Newton–Schulz evaluations, and MLLM-DCL EBO results.

M1.justification: Appendix B.4 adds an evaluated Newton–Schulz alternative to eigendecomposition-based whitening, approximately enforcing orthonormality through iterative matrix multiplication. The main EBLoRA factorization, gradient projections, and initialization remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use UCIT, MLLM-DCL, and MM-MergeBench with the same represented datasets and tasks. The added experiments evaluate variants within this existing coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds the free-spectrum U_t S_t V_t^T comparator against EBO on UCIT and extends EBO ablation reporting to MLLM-DCL. The main comparisons retain LoRA-FT, O-LoRA, CL-MoE, SEFE, and KeepLoRA.

E3.justification: The added experiments introduce free-spectrum and Newton–Schulz configurations, wall-clock time per iteration, peak GPU memory, and an arithmetic mean of MFN, MAA, BWT, and FWT. Existing benchmark settings, learning rates, epoch limits, and original metric definitions are unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 adds a control separating spectral balancing from orthogonal parameterization. Appendix B.4 adds computational-cost and approximate-retraction analyses, while Table 8 extends the EBO component ablation to MLLM-DCL. Together these substantially expand examination of the mechanism and its practical tradeoffs.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the experimental results. The retained singular-value variance analysis describes spectral structure rather than statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: Existing main and matched appendix results remain unchanged, but v2 adds substantive mechanism and efficiency findings. Table 4 reports UCIT MFN 68.1 for the free-spectrum variant versus EBO's 70.2; Table 6 reports 71.6 for Newton–Schulz versus retained EBLoRA's 72.8. Table 8 adds MLLM-DCL EBO MFN 62.1, and Table 5 newly quantifies training-time and memory overhead.

T1.justification: Propositions 3.1–3.2 and their Appendix A proofs are unchanged. Appendix B.4 adds the Newton–Schulz recurrence and reasoning that its iterates preserve the gradient-null-space constraint while approximately satisfying orthonormality, plus a definition of the new mean aggregate score.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about spectral imbalance, balanced low-rank updates, restricted-Stiefel optimization, forgetting reduction, and preserved plasticity. The additions supply supporting evidence without redefining these core claims.

C2.justification: v2 newly interprets the free-spectrum results as evidence that orthogonal parameterization helps but explicit spectral balance provides additional gains. Appendix B.4 discusses computational overhead and qualifies Newton–Schulz as a faster alternative with slightly lower final performance.

D1.justification: Appendix B.4 adds measured training times, peak memory usage, and Newton–Schulz initialization and update details, although its iteration count is unspecified. Existing hardware, training hyperparameters, GPM settings, and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations including LADA, DC-Merge, selective parameter updating, and Newton–Schulz/polar-decomposition sources, and removes Boothby (1975). Related-work descriptions receive limited edits; the central research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most wording and section order are retained. Changes include a geometric explanation, the free-spectrum discussion, Appendix B.4, acknowledgements, updated correspondence and venue text, and small terminology edits.

P2.justification: v2 adds the manifold illustration in Figure 3 and four tables covering the free-spectrum control, costs, Newton–Schulz, and MLLM-DCL EBO results. Existing displays retain their designs; appendix tables are locally reordered and subsequent figures and tables renumbered.

improvement.justification: The free-spectrum control strengthens attribution of gains to spectral balance, while cost measurements and the Newton–Schulz evaluation clarify practical tradeoffs. These targeted improvements preserve the original evidence. A small new reporting inconsistency tempers the gain: Table 8 reports FWT 32.5, although its entries yield approximately 32.9 under Equation 21.
